subject: Transient P95 drift — Transitly production impact & mitigation
messages:
From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@transitly.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production P95 spike — seeing 4x on text-gen

Hi Mina,

We're seeing a P95 jump on our test namespace starting ~07:45 PT that correlates with longer tail token generation times. This is impacting near-real-time features for our rider ETA predictions (30–45s for some requests vs usual ~2s). Attached a small trace and one example payload.

Any known deploys or routing changes at Redwood? Our team rolled nothing on our side. Impacting ~3% of traffic but noticeably affecting QA and a handful of production requests.

Thanks — please escalate if needed.

—Rajesh
Rajesh Patel
Head of Engineering — Transitly

Subject: Re: Production P95 spike — seeing 4x on text-gen

Initial triage notes (quick):
- No control-plane deploys in the last 2 hours.
- Metrics show token-level scheduling latency increase starting 07:42 PT across three DGs serving Transitly.
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% for the affected model (gpt-lite-3b-q4_0).
- GPU utilization is normal; queues on the inference scheduler increased for sequence lengths >512.

Actioning: collecting kernel traces and requesting a log bundle (Sean). If KV evaporation confirmed, we'll consider short-term cache-warm and a canary to gpt-lite-3b-q2 (smaller quant) as fallback.

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh@transitly.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production P95 spike — seeing 4x on text-gen

Uploading the log bundle to the shared drive now (attached here as transitly-logs-20280318.tar.gz). Excerpt below (sanitized):

--- start excerpt ---
[07:43:12] scheduler: dispatch_delay_ms p95=3100 (baseline p95=120)
[07:43:13] kvcache: eviction_rate spike -> misses increased by 14%
[07:43:14] kernel-selection: fallback to generic-attn (slower path) observed
--- end excerpt ---

Preliminary hypothesis: a burst of long-context requests caused a cache eviction window and triggered the generic-attn kernel path for some model shards. That combination explains both queueing and per-token slowdown.

Requesting product input on safe fallback: if we can route ~25% of Transitly traffic to gpt-lite-3b-q2 for 15–30 mins, we can reduce tail latency while we warm caches. Need Marissa's signoff and Mina to confirm with Transitly.

Sean
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh@transitly.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production P95 spike — seeing 4x on text-gen

Thanks team — product stance: safe fallback to a compatible quantized variant is acceptable for short windows if performance improves and we annotate outputs with the model tag. Constraints:
- Avoid changes that alter token-level semantics for more than 1% of requests (Transitly SLA).
- Notify Transitly with a short behavioral note and expected revert window.

Marissa: can we do a controlled canary (25% -> 50% ramp) for 20 minutes and monitor per-customer regression against our eval set for Transitly (I’ll trigger a quick smoke eval)?

I’ll prepare a short product-approved blurb for Mina to send to Transitly with the plan, risks, and rollback criteria.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@transitly.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Action plan: temporary canary + monitoring (Transitly)

Hi Rajesh — updating you on our plan to mitigate the P95 spike: 

1) What we’ll do (15:40 PT start window; ~20–30 minute test): route 25% of Transitly production traffic for the affected model to gpt-lite-3b-q2 (quantized variant) as a short-term canary. This should reduce tail latency while we warm the KV cache.
2) Monitoring: SRE will monitor token-level P50/P95, per-request failure rate, and a quick behavioral smoke eval run by Product. If any regression >1% or errors increase, we’ll immediately rollback.
3) Why this is safe: the fallback model is functionally compatible; Marissa’s team will tag responses as from the fallback model for telemetry.

We plan to start within the hour. Attaching logs we collected for your ops team. Will follow up with a short note after the canary window with observed numbers.

Questions/concerns? If you’re okay, reply with ACK and we’ll proceed.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@transitly.com>, Transitly Ops <ops@transitly.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2028 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-canary update: P95 improved, follow-ups

Rajesh / Transitly ops — quick update from the short canary we ran yesterday evening:

- Canary window: 2028-03-18 15:42–16:05 PT, 25% traffic to gpt-lite-3b-q2.
- Observed: token-level P95 dropped from ~31s -> ~2.3s on canary path; end-to-end observed user-facing P95 for Transitly reduced from 41s -> 3.1s overall.
- No functional regressions detected in Marissa's smoke eval (regression <0.4%).
- We reverted after the 23-minute window; caches are warming — KV hit rate currently recovering (+9% vs baseline).

Attachments: transitly-logs-20280318.tar.gz, slo-uptime-report-Q1-2028.pdf.

Next steps:
- Karthik/Sean to continue watching KV hit-rate and kernel-selection metrics for 48h.
- Product (Marissa) to add a short canary guidance item to the roadmap: "short fallback windows for cache-evaporation events" (we'll sync on priority).
- Mina will send a formal incident summary to Transitly in next 24h and coordinate any billing/SLA questions with Vanessa.

Thanks — please flag any outstanding asks.

—Mina
